Quit every Hermes process on this profile (Desktop app, `hermes {profile_arg}gateway stop`, dashboard, cron), run `hermes {profile_arg}doctor` — it names any process still holding the log — then start Hermes again and send your message once more. gateway.topic.help:
/topic — enable multi-session DM mode (one bot, many parallel chats)

Usage:
  /topic             Enable topic mode, or show status if already on
  /topic help        Show this message
  /topic off         Disable topic mode and clear topic bindings
  /topic <id>        Inside a topic: restore a previous session by ID

How it works:
1. Run /topic once in this DM — Hermes checks BotFather Threads
   Settings are enabled and flips on multi-session mode.
2. Tap All Messages at the top of the bot and send any message.
   Telegram creates a new topic for that message; each topic is
   an independent Hermes session (fresh history, fresh context).
3. The root DM becomes a system lobby — send /topic, /status,
   /help, /usage there. Normal prompts go in a topic.
4. /new inside a topic resets just that topic's session.
5. /topic <id> inside a topic restores an old session into it.

slash.redraw.description: Force a full UI repaint (recovers from terminal drift)
slash.refine.description: Review this conversation now and save lessons to memory/skills
slash.reload-skills.description: Re-scan ~/.hermes/skills/ for newly installed or removed skills
slash.reload.description: Reload .env variables into the running session
slash.restart.description: Gracefully restart the gateway after draining active runs
slash.retry.description: Retry the last message (resend to agent)
slash.review.description: Spawn an independent subagent to review the work just discussed (PR, code, docs)
slash.rollback.description: List or restore filesystem checkpoints (restores keep your hand-edits; --all overrides)
slash.save.description: Export the current conversation (bare /save shows usage)
slash.sethome.description: Set this chat as the home channel
slash.skills.description: Search, install, inspect, or manage skills
slash.skin.description: Show or change the display skin/theme
slash.snapshot.description: Create or restore state snapshots of Hermes config/state
slash.start.description: Acknowledge platform start pings without a reply
slash.status.description: Show session, model, token, and context info
slash.steer.description: Inject a message after the next tool call without interrupting
slash.subgoal.description: Add or manage extra criteria on the active goal
slash.subscription.description: View your Nous plan and change it in the browser
slash.title.description: Set a title for the current session
slash.topic.description: Enable or inspect Telegram DM topic sessions
slash.topup.description: Show your Nous balance and manage billing on the portal
slash.undo.description: Back up N user turns and re-prompt (default 1)
slash.update.description: Update Hermes Agent to the latest version
slash.usage.description: Show token usage and rate limits; `reset` redeems a banked Codex limit reset
slash.verbose.description: Cycle tool progress display: off -> new -> all -> verbose
slash.wake.description: Toggle the 'Hey Hermes' wake word listener
slash.whoami.description: Show your slash command access (admin / user)
slash.worktree.description: Show, list, create, or prune isolated git worktrees
slash.yolo.description: Toggle YOLO mode (skip all dangerous command approvals)

tips.t264: When compression fails, further attempts are paused for 10 minutes to avoid API hammering.
tips.t265: Long dangerous commands (>70 chars) get a 'view' option in the approval prompt to see the full text first.
tips.t266: Audio level visualization shows ▁▂▃▄▅▆▇ bars during voice recording based on microphone RMS levels.
tips.t267: Profile names cannot collide with existing PATH binaries — 'hermes profile create ls' would be rejected.
tips.t268: hermes profile create backup --clone-all copies everything (config, keys, SOUL.md, memories, skills, sessions).
tips.t269: The voice record key is configurable via voice.record_key in config.yaml — not just Ctrl+B.
tips.t270: .cursorrules and .cursor/rules/*.mdc files are auto-detected and loaded as project context.
tips.t271: Context files support 10+ prompt injection patterns — invisible Unicode, 'ignore instructions', exfil attempts.
tips.t272: GPT-5 and Codex use 'developer' role instead of 'system' in the message format.
tips.t273: Per-task auxiliary overrides: auxiliary.vision.provider, auxiliary.compression.model, etc. in config.yaml.
tips.t274: The auxiliary client treats 'main' as a provider alias — resolves to your actual primary provider + model.
tips.t275: hermes claw migrate --dry-run previews OpenClaw migration without writing anything.
tips.t276: File paths pasted with quotes or escaped spaces are handled automatically — no manual cleanup needed.
tips.t277: Slash commands never trigger the large-paste collapse — /command with big arguments works correctly.
tips.t278: In interrupt mode, slash commands typed during agent execution bypass interrupt logic and run immediately.
tips.t279: HERMES_DEV=1 bypasses container mode detection for local development.
tips.t280: Each MCP server gets its own toolset (mcp-servername) that can be toggled independently via hermes tools.
tips.t281: MCP ${ENV_VAR} placeholders in config are resolved at server spawn — including vars from ~/.hermes/.env.
tips.t282: Skills from trusted repos (NousResearch) get a 'trusted' security level; community skills get extra scanning.
tips.t283: The skills quarantine at ~/.hermes/skills/.hub/quarantine/ holds skills pending security review.
tips.t284: /steer <prompt> injects a note after the next tool call — nudge direction mid-task without interrupting.
tips.t285: /goal <text> sets a standing Ralph-loop objective — Hermes auto-continues turn after turn until a judge says done.
tips.t286: /snapshot create [label] saves a full state snapshot of Hermes config; /snapshot restore <id> reverts later.
tips.t287: /copy [N] copies the last assistant response to your clipboard, or the Nth-from-last with a number.
tips.t288: /redraw forces a full UI repaint, fixing terminal drift after tmux resize or mouse selection artifacts.
tips.t289: /agents (alias /tasks) shows active agents and running background tasks across the current session.
tips.t290: /footer toggles the gateway footer on final replies showing model, context %, and cwd.
tips.t291: /busy queue|steer|interrupt controls what pressing Enter does while Hermes is working.
tips.t292: /topic in Telegram DMs enables user-managed multi-session topic mode — /topic <id> restores past sessions inline.
tips.t293: /approve session|always runs a pending dangerous command with your chosen trust scope; /deny rejects it.
tips.t294: /restart gracefully restarts the gateway after draining active runs, then pings the requester when back up.
tips.t295: /kanban boards switch <slug> changes the active multi-project Kanban board from inside chat.
tips.t296: /reload reloads ~/.hermes/.env into the running session — pick up new API keys without restarting.
tips.t297: cronjob with no_agent=True runs a script on schedule and sends its stdout directly — zero tokens, zero LLM.
tips.t298: An empty cron script stdout means silent tick — nothing is delivered, perfect for threshold watchdogs.
tips.t299: HERMES_CRON_MAX_PARALLEL (default 4) caps how many cron jobs run per tick so bursts don't saturate your keys.
tips.t300: Gateway hooks live under ~/.hermes/hooks/<name>/ with HOOK.yaml + handler.py — handler must be named `handle`.
tips.t301: Hook events include gateway:startup, session:start, agent:step, and command:* wildcard subscriptions.
tips.t302: Drop a ~/.hermes/BOOT.md checklist and a gateway:startup hook runs it as a one-shot agent every boot.
tips.t303: hermes curator run --dry-run previews what the curator would archive or consolidate without mutating anything.
tips.t304: hermes curator pin <skill> hard-fences a skill against both auto-archival and the agent's skill_manage tool.
tips.t305: hermes curator rollback restores skills from a pre-run snapshot — backups live under skills/.curator_backups/.
tips.t306: hermes auth reset <provider> [target] clears cooldowns and exhaustion flags on a whole credential pool, or on one credential by index, id, or label.
tips.t307: credential_pool_strategies.<provider>: round_robin cycles keys evenly instead of the fill_first default.
tips.t308: use_gateway: true per-tool routes web, image, tts, or browser through your Nous subscription — no extra keys.
tips.t309: provider_routing.data_collection: deny excludes data-storing providers on OpenRouter.
tips.t310: provider_routing.require_parameters: true only routes to providers that support every param in your request.
tips.t311: HERMES_TUI_RESUME=1 auto-re-attaches to the most recent TUI session on launch — handy after SSH drops.
tips.t312: HERMES_TUI_THEME=light|dark|<hex> forces the TUI theme on terminals that don't set COLORFGBG.
tips.t313: Ctrl+G or Ctrl+X Ctrl+E in the TUI opens the input buffer in $EDITOR for long multi-line prompts.
tips.t314: The TUI renders LaTeX inline — $E=mc^2$ becomes Unicode math instead of raw TeX.
tips.t315: hermes dashboard launches a local web UI at 127.0.0.1:9119 — zero data leaves localhost.
tips.t316: hermes dashboard embeds the full Hermes TUI in your browser via xterm.js and a WebSocket PTY.
tips.t317: Drop a YAML in ~/.hermes/dashboard-themes/ with two palette colors to reskin the entire dashboard.
tips.t318: Dashboard plugins are drop-in: manifest.json + JS bundle in ~/.hermes/dashboard-plugins/ — no npm build required.
tips.t319: layoutVariant: cockpit in a dashboard theme adds a 260px left rail that plugins can populate via the sidebar slot.
tips.t320: display.tool_progress_command: true exposes /verbose on messaging platforms; it's CLI-only by default.
tips.t321: HERMES_BACKGROUND_NOTIFICATIONS=result only pings when background tasks finish (vs concise/all/error/off).
tips.t322: HERMES_WRITE_SAFE_ROOT restricts write_file/patch to directory prefixes; multiple paths via os.pathsep (: or ;).
tips.t323: HERMES_IGNORE_RULES skips auto-injection of AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, .cursorrules, memory, and preloaded skills.
tips.t324: HERMES_ACCEPT_HOOKS auto-approves unseen shell hooks declared in config.yaml without a TTY prompt.
tips.t325: auxiliary.goal_judge.model routes the /goal judge to a cheap fast model to keep loop cost near zero.
tips.t326: Checkpoints skip directories with more than 50,000 files to avoid slow git operations on massive monorepos.
tips.t327: tts.provider: piper runs 44-language local TTS on CPU — voices auto-download to ~/.hermes/cache/piper-voices/.
tips.t328: tts.providers.<name>.type: command wires any CLI TTS engine with {input_path} and {output_path} placeholders.
tips.t329: API_SERVER_ENABLED=true runs an OpenAI-compatible endpoint alongside the gateway for Open WebUI and LibreChat.
tips.t330: GATEWAY_PROXY_URL runs a split setup: platform I/O locally, agent work delegated to a remote API server.
tips.t331: MATRIX_DEVICE_ID pins a stable device ID for E2EE — without it, keys rotate every start and historic decrypt breaks.
tips.t332: TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is required whenever TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_URL is set — generate with openssl rand -hex 32.
tips.t333: batch_runner.py --resume content-matches completed prompts by text so dataset reorders don't re-run finished work.
tips.t334: /new starts a fresh session in place (alias /reset) — fresh session ID, clean history, CLI stays open.
tips.t335: /clear wipes the terminal screen AND starts a new session — one shortcut for a visual reset.
tips.t336: /history prints the current conversation in-line without leaving the CLI — useful for a quick re-read.
tips.t337: /save writes the current conversation to disk without ending the session.
tips.t338: /status shows session info at a glance: ID, title, model, token usage, and elapsed time.
tips.t339: /image <path> attaches a local image file for your next prompt without pasting or drag-and-drop.
tips.t340: /platforms shows gateway and messaging-platform connection status right from inside chat.
tips.t341: /commands paginates the full slash-command + installed-skill list — useful on platforms without tab completion.
tips.t342: /toolsets lists every available toolset so you know what -t/--toolsets accepts.
tips.t343: /voice tts toggles TTS-only mode — agent replies out loud but you still type your prompts.
tips.t344: /reload-skills re-scans ~/.hermes/skills/ so drop-in skills appear without restarting the session.
tips.t345: /indicator kaomoji|emoji|unicode|ascii picks the TUI busy-indicator style shown during agent runs.
tips.t346: /debug uploads a support bundle (system info + logs) and returns shareable links — works in chat too.
tips.t347: hermes -z "<prompt>" is the purest one-shot: final answer on stdout, nothing else — ideal for piping in scripts.
tips.t348: hermes chat --pass-session-id injects the session ID into the system prompt so the agent can self-reference it.
tips.t349: hermes chat --image path/to/pic.png attaches a local image to a single -q query without a separate upload step.
tips.t350: hermes chat --ignore-user-config skips the active user config — reproducible bug reports and CI runs.
tips.t351: hermes chat --source tool tags programmatic chats so they don't clutter hermes sessions list.
tips.t352: hermes dump --show-keys includes redacted API key fingerprints for deeper support debugging.
tips.t353: hermes sessions rename <ID> "new title" renames any past session; hermes sessions delete <ID> removes one.
tips.t354: hermes import restores a full Hermes backup zip; session JSON/JSONL exports import from the dashboard Sessions page.
tips.t355: hermes fallback manages the fallback_model chain interactively — no hand-editing config.yaml.
tips.t356: hermes pairing rotates the DM pairing token — the first messager after rotation claims access to the bot.
tips.t357: hermes setup walks first-time users through provider, keys, and platform wiring in one interactive flow.
tips.t358: hermes status --deep runs the full health sweep across every component; plain hermes status is the quick view.
tips.t359: HERMES_AGENT_TIMEOUT=0 disables the gateway inactivity kill for a running agent — use for long research runs.
tips.t360: HERMES_ENABLE_PROJECT_PLUGINS=1 auto-loads repo-local plugins from ./.hermes/plugins/ — trust-gated by design.
tips.t361: HERMES_DISABLE_FILE_STATE_GUARD=1 turns off the 'file changed since you read it' guard on patch and write_file.
tips.t362: HERMES_ALLOW_PRIVATE_URLS=true lets web tools hit localhost and private networks — off by default in gateway mode.
tips.t363: HERMES_OPTIONAL_SKILLS=name1,name2 auto-installs extra optional-catalog skills on first run per profile.
tips.t364: HERMES_BUNDLED_SKILLS points at a custom bundled-skill tree — used by Homebrew and Nix packaging.
tips.t365: HERMES_DUMP_REQUEST_STDOUT=1 dumps every API request payload to stdout instead of log files.
tips.t366: HERMES_OAUTH_TRACE=1 logs redacted OAuth token exchange and refresh attempts for debugging provider auth.
tips.t367: HERMES_STREAM_RETRIES (default 3) controls mid-stream reconnect attempts on transient network errors.
tips.t368: HERMES_GATEWAY_BUSY_ACK_ENABLED=false silences the ⚡/⏳/⏩ ack messages when a user messages a busy agent.
tips.t369: HERMES_AGENT_NOTIFY_INTERVAL (default 180s) sets how often the gateway pings with progress on long turns.
tips.t370: HERMES_RESTART_DRAIN_TIMEOUT (default 900s) caps how long /restart waits for in-flight runs before forcing.
tips.t371: HERMES_CHECKPOINT_TIMEOUT (default 30s) caps filesystem checkpoint creation — raise it on huge monorepos.
tips.t372: image_gen.model in config.yaml picks the FAL model: flux-2/klein, gpt-image-2, nano-banana-pro, and more.
tips.t373: image_gen.provider routes image generation through a plugin (OpenAI Images, Codex, FAL) instead of the default.
tips.t374: AUXILIARY_VISION_BASE_URL + AUXILIARY_VISION_API_KEY point vision analysis at any OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
tips.t375: API_SERVER_MODEL_NAME customizes the model name on /v1/models — essential for multi-profile Open WebUI setups.
tips.t376: Dashboard plugins are served from /dashboard-plugins/<name>/ — drop files into ~/.hermes/dashboard-plugins/.
tips.t377: --source tool chats are excluded from hermes sessions list by default — set --source explicitly to see them.
